{{Top|rwm|can|fotj}} {{Otheruses|Academy}} {{TelevisionEpisode |image=[[File:Epguide306.jpg]] |title="The Academy" |series=''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode306.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: The Academy}} |season=[[The Clone Wars: Season Three|Three]] |episode=6 |production=2.26 |screener= |airdate=[[October 15]], [[2010]] |intl release= |runtime=25 minutes |director=[[Giancarlo Volpe]] |writer=*[[Katie Lucas]] *[[Steven Melching]] |production company= |guests= |canon_timeline=[[21 BBY]]{{TCWcanondates|306}} |legends_timeline=[[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]]{{TCWdates|306}} |prev="[[Corruption (episode)|Corruption]]" |next="[[Assassin (episode)|Assassin]]" }} {{Quote|Those who enforce the law must obey the law.|Moral|{{TCW|The Academy}}}} "'''The Academy'''" is the sixth episode of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series' [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|third season]]. It aired on [[October 15]], [[2010]] and concluded a two-part storyline started with the previous episode, "[[Corruption (episode)|Corruption]]." ==Official description== ''Ahsoka Tano is assigned to teach a class at a leadership academy on Mandalore. Soon after she arrives, Duchess Satine's zealous nephew -- Korkie Kryze -- and his classmates uncover a nefarious plot. Prime Minister Almec is revealed to be an active part of the Mandalorian black market conspiracy on Mandalore, and he attempts to permanently silence Duchess Satine and the cadets before they expose his corruption. Ahsoka and the cadets defeat Almec before he can succeed.'' ==Opening narration== {{OpeningCrawl |name=Episode 6
THE ACADEMY |text=A world in crisis! The peaceful planet of Mandalore is being strangled by the grip of corruption. With shortages of every kind, citizens must turn to the black market in order to survive. Desperate to free her people, Duchess Satine has asked her friend Padmé Amidala to speak with the Jedi Council in hopes that they will send assistance to her struggling world....}} ==Plot summary== {{Quote|Looks like the Academy taught us well.|Korkie|}} [[Anakin Skywalker]] escorts his [[Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano]] to [[Mandalore]] for her undercover assignment: to investigate the corruption within the government and also to teach aspiring cadets the ways of lawful and public-serving conduct. She was chosen specifically so, by her status as a learner and her youth, she could serve as a role model for the students. At the landing platform the two are welcomed by [[Duchess]] [[Satine Kryze|Satine]] herself, [[Prime Minister]] [[Almec]], and the [[cadet]]s [[Korkie Kryze|Korkie]] (the Duchess' own nephew), [[Amis]] and [[Lagos]]. Due to [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]]'s previous encounters with the [[Death Watch]] on the planet, a no-weapons order has been issued, and Ahsoka is forced to surrender her [[lightsaber]] to her master, who leaves to rendezvous with fellow [[Jedi]] [[Kit Fisto]]. Ahsoka begins teaching classes, including Korkie and his friends, about the nature of corruption and their duty as lawful citizens to combat it. Later that evening, Korkie, Amis, Lagos, and [[Soniee]] talk about Ahsoka's lesson and Korkie muses over the rationing of the Academy's [[Foodstuff|food]] supplies. They sneak off to a warehouse and stumble upon a clandestine meeting between three [[Mandalorian]] officers, three [[Gotal]]s, and a [[humanoid]] figure wreathed in a robe and hood, who unfortunately has his back turned to the young cadets. They manage to get a [[Holocamera|holocam]] recording, but a blunder by Amis exposes the quartet; they narrowly manage to leave, but Soniee's laptop terminal is found by the conspirators. The next morning, the cadets visit Satine and report their discovery. While Satine believes them, she cautions them to hold back as they are still too young and untrained for this sort of thing, suspecting that the conspiracy runs even deeper. The cadets do not take this dismissal kindly and choose to ask Almec for help. In class, Ahsoka notices that the four are distracted and learns of their plans, but her own well-meaning words of caution dispirits the young cadets even more. The same night, as the cadets prepare to meet with the Prime Minister, they are met by members of the [[Mandalorian secret service]], who attempt to arrest them for [[treason]] and conspiracy, but Ahsoka steps in and drives them away. Using [[information retrieval]] to analyze the holo-recording of the warehouse meeting, the cadets and Ahsoka discover to their surprise that the cloaked figure from the warehouse is Almec himself. As the five rush off to inform Satine, they find her missing and her bodyguards dead. Desperate, the cadets turn to Ahsoka for leadership, who devises a cunning plan: by pretending that she has arrested the cadets and voicing the suspicion that Satine is involved, she gains Almec's trust, but fails to learn of the Duchess' whereabouts. While Almec leaves to prepare a public statement, Ahsoka enters the prison under the pretense of wanting to conduct an interrogation, informs the cadets about the changes in her plan, and via a [[Mind trick|Force mind trick]] makes one of the guards take her to Satine's cell. However, the guards prove in reality to be resistant to Jedi mind tricks; Almec had set up the situation as a trap, and Ahsoka is hit by a [[stun]] blast and captured. Almec proceeds to gloat over having established the [[black market]] system on Mandalore, self-indulgently claiming it was done out of humanitarian considerations. He [[Shock collar|tries to make]] the Duchess sign a confession of treason, which she refuses, so Almec has Korkie and the others brought to him to persuade her otherwise. When he prepares to have Korkie fit with a shock collar, Ahsoka and the cadets start a fight, and though outnumbered and handcuffed, they manage to overpower the guards and clamp a shock collar on Almec himself, forcing him to give up. After the conspirators are arrested, Ahsoka departs from her new friends, following her master back into [[Clone Wars|the war]] while exchanging a few of their usual snippy comments about her assignment. ==Continuity== The Mandalorian prison guards have a crest upon their shoulder that reads "In Defense of Mandalore." It is written in a [[Mandalorian (writing system)|Mandalorian typeface]] developed for the ''[[Slave I]]'' display screens in ''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones''. The full text of the lesson shown behind Ahsoka Tano reads as follows:
"This graph represents corruption related crimes within Mandalore.
'''Types of corruption involve:'''
''- Bribery''
The offering of something which is most often money but can also be goods or services in order to gain an unfair advantage.
''- Extortion''
Threatening or inflicting harm to a person, their reputation, or their property in order to obtain money, actions, services, or other goods from that person.
''- Embezzlement''
The illegal taking or appropriation of money or property that has been entrusted to a person but is actually owned by another.
''- Nepotism''
The practice or inclination to favor a person or group who is a relative or friend when giving promotions, jobs, raises, and other benefits to employees.
''- Patronage Systems''
The granting of favors, contracts, or appointments to positions by a local public office holder or candidate for a political office in return for political support.
'''Corruption in Mandalore'''
Since the turn of the century corruption has been on the rise. And now with the current changes in the Mandalorian government and the rebellion of the Death Watch, corruption is only expected to increase. One must be educated about corruption in order to prevent it. Take action and do your part to stop corruption."
